validity.recommendation: Adjudicate P3962 against the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline (Petroline) system and the Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL pipeline GEM entities before keeping it as a distinct gas row; it most likely double-counts the Petroline 48-inch leg. Candidate merge/removal.
validity.researcher_notes: P3962's backend specs (LengthKnown=1200 km, Diameter=48 in) exactly match the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline (Petroline), which independent sources give as 1,201 km comprising two lines — one 56-inch (crude) and one 48-inch that was 'originally for natural gas liquids' (en.wikipedia East-West Crude Oil Pipeline). The gem.wiki page for P3962 itself carries an EMPTY infobox (no length, diameter, capacity or start year) and states in the Background that it 'runs parallel to the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline' and lists that crude line as 'Associated infrastructure' — so the 1200/48 numbers were not on the page and appear imported from the Petroline. GEM already tracks the Petroline system as 'East-West Crude Oil Pipeline' (crude, GOIT) and the parallel NGL line as 'Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL pipeline' (1,171 km, 290,000 bpd NGL, start 1982). P3962 is therefore very likely a relabel/double-count of the Petroline's 48-inch leg (and/or the Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL line), not an independent physical gas trunk. GulfPub lists an 'East-West Gas Pipeline | operating | Abqaiq/Shedgum -> Yanbu' at 727 km — a different length again, none of which support 1200 km for a gas line. Existence of the east-west corridor is real; the distinct GAS entity is the problem.

validity.recommendation: If P3962 corresponds to the Petroline 48-inch leg, it is NOT natural-gas transmission: that leg originally carried NGL and per Wikipedia was 'converted to carry crude oil'. Reclassify (NGL/crude -> GOIT) or delete as duplicate. Do not treat Fuel=Gas as sourced.
validity.researcher_notes: The Fuel [ref] and PipelineType [ref] cells cite al-madina article 862300, whose title translates to 'Petroline: an OIL (نفطي) project linking the east of the Kingdom with its west' — an explicitly CRUDE OIL Petroline article, not a gas source. The Status [ref] cites archive.aramcoworld 198206 'Foundations: The Keystone', a 1982 Petroline (crude) construction article (verifier: 200 but 'operating' not present). The 48-inch line of the East-West system was 'originally for natural gas liquids' and, per Wikipedia, the accompanying NGL pipelines 'were converted to carry crude oil' — so neither historically nor currently is it a methane gas-transmission trunk. Fuel=Gas / PipelineType=transmission (as a GGIT gas line) is unsupported by the row's own sources, which all describe crude/NGL.

validity.recommendation: Do not keep LengthKnown=1200 km or Diameter=48 in as gas-line specs — they are the crude Petroline's numbers. Any surviving gas/NGL entity should carry its own sourced length (NGL ~1,171 km; GulfPub gas ~727 km; 2014 Saipem Shedgum-Yanbu NGL ~585 km). Leave blank pending merge decision.
validity.researcher_notes: 1200 km + 48 in are the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline's figures (1,201 km; 48-inch leg). No independent source gives 1,200 km / 48 in for a Saudi east-west GAS line. Competing independent gas/NGL lengths: Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL = 1,171 km; GulfPub 'East-West Gas Pipeline' = 727 km; 2014 Saipem Shedgum-Yanbu NGL contract = 585 km / 30 in (Argaam). These disagree materially with each other and with 1200/48, confirming the GEM values were lifted from the crude pipeline rather than sourced for a gas line. StartYear1=1978 is loosely supported (techint 2023 'Shedgum-Yanbu ... 45 years of history' -> ~1978) but the crude/NGL system is more commonly dated to commissioning 1982.

routes.start_name: Abqaiq / Shedgum gas-oil separation & processing area, Eastern Province
routes.end_name: Yanbu (Yanbu al-Bahr), Red Sea coast, Al Madinah Province

waypoints.name: Central Najd / south of Riyadh (approximate corridor midpoint — alignment not sourced to meters)

routes.corridor_desc: The east-west corridor runs from Aramco's Abqaiq/Shedgum processing area in the Eastern Province roughly west-northwest across the central Najd plateau (passing to the south of Riyadh) to the Yanbu industrial/oil-terminal complex on the Red Sea coast — the same corridor as the Petroline (East-West Crude Oil Pipeline) and the parallel Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL line, which this row appears to duplicate. Endpoints are well established (named cities/facilities); the intermediate alignment is a loose corridor, not a surveyed route.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints Abqaiq/Shedgum (Eastern Province) -> Yanbu (Red Sea) are corroborated by Wikipedia (Abqaiq -> Yanbu Oil Terminal) and Argaam/GulfPub (Shedgum -> Yanbu). Coordinates are approximate centroids of the named cities/facilities (Abqaiq ~25.94N 49.66E; Shedgum ~25.36N 49.36E; Yanbu ~24.09N 38.06E) — real place coordinates, not fabricated; no interior waypoint coordinate is asserted because the exact alignment is not independently sourced. NOTE: this corridor is shared with the Petroline and NGL lines this row likely duplicates — resolve identity before treating as a distinct route.

summary: P3962 East-West Gas Pipeline is a concern: its 1200 km/48 in specs are the crude Petroline's 48-inch (originally-NGL, now-crude) leg — likely a duplicate/misclassification of the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline and/or Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL line, not a distinct operating gas trunk.
